correctness.rationale: The self-contained checker reconstructs all 15 Petersen graph edges from disjoint 2-subsets of [5], enumerates all 2^15 edge subsets (10870 allowed including empty), verifies the ten-entry f-vector and a 5432-pair greedy toggle matching; a directed-Hasse acyclicity topological sort visits every nonempty face with 63780 cover relations, leaving exactly one critical 0-face and four critical 7-faces. Hence homology is concentrated in degree seven with rank four. For all 120 ground-letter permutations, the signed edge-orbit sum matches fixed letters minus one, and an independent oriented-fixed-simplex Lefschetz calculation confirms all seven conjugacy-class representatives. The semisimple rational character equals the standard quotient character; a character self-inner product of one confirms irreducibility.

originality.rationale: The exact same-object published record establishes only a four-sphere wedge, which fixes the rational homology dimension but cannot determine an S5-character. The new signed Lefschetz calculation gives seven exact conjugacy-class traces, identifies the standard irreducible and proves no invariant classes. The inspected published graph-family theorems, cut-complex representation and configuration-space results neither state nor imply this module. Search limits remain.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently termed equivalent S5-character computation could exist; finite published-finding corpus and web search is not a mathematical proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical S5-symmetric cubic graph and its higher matching complex is already known only nonequivariantly; identifying a natural four-dimensional homology as the irreducible standard S5 module is a complete action-level classification. It detects zero global invariant classes and distinguishes the natural action from other possible four-dimensional actions. This precise representation is not determined by homotopy/Betti numbers and is a motivated symmetry refinement rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
